newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's ABS-CBN, advertisers compromise on rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila's ABS-CBN, advertisers compromise on rates.

text.p: Philippine television network ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp has reached a compromise with a group of advertisers over an increase in primetime advertising rates, an advertising agency group said on Thursday.
The boost in rates ranges from 18.6 to 21 percent, the Association of Accredited Advertising Agencies (4As) said.

Last week, the network's proposed increase in rates to 22 percent triggered a protest by the Philippine Association of National Advertisers (Pana), which then cancelled advertising slots from March 10.
Pana had said it would accept a 15 percent increase in rates.
Oscar Valenzuela, president of the 4As, told Reuters by phone on Thursday that the agreement was finalised on Tuesday and the rates vary depending on the programme's timeslot and rating.
The new rates have been accepted by Pana, he said.
An ABS-CBN official, who asked not to be identified, said that the company could not comment on the issue as it had agreed for the advertisers to make the announcement.
Pana, with the support of 4As, had threatened to continue its boycott of the television station until the issue was resolved.
Pana is made up of 302 advertisers which include stock market heavyweights San Miguel Corp, Petron Corp, Ayala Corp and Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co.
ABS-CBN said on Monday that although advertisements dropped by 23 percent from March 10 to 12, some advertisers came back late last week.
